Definition: from G575 and στερέω (to deprive); to despoil:--defraud, destitute, kept back by fraud.
BiblicalUsage: The word means to defraud, to keep back what belongs to someone else. Paul tells the Corinthians they already lose by going to law against each other, because they wrong and defraud their own brothers; married couples are not to defraud one another except by agreement for prayer; and the commandments themselves forbid it.
TheologicalSignificance: I hold that defrauding a brother is worse than losing a lawsuit. God sees the quiet keeping-back, in money and in marriage, and He calls it what it is.
